inputs.title: Source
inputs.tooltip: The price the filter tracks. Close is the usual choice. HL2 or OHLC4 average the whole bar, so a close that lands at one extreme of the bar counts for less.

inputs.title: Trend Smoothness
inputs.tooltip: How smooth the filter line is, read like a moving-average period. Higher gives a smoother line that lags price more. Lower keeps the line closer to price but lets more noise through.

inputs.title: Surprise Meter
inputs.tooltip:
Innovation is the standard Kalman filter term for the gap between where the filter predicted price would land and where it actually landed. You can think of it as surprise. Every bar the filter makes a forecast, like a weather forecast calling for 70 degrees, and the surprise is how far off it was when the real number came in.

The Surprise meter is drawn above zero. It compares recent surprises to what the filter normally expects. 0 means price is landing about where the filter expects. 50 means surprises are running at twice their normal level, 75 means four times. It jumps at a shock and fades as the shock passes.

The color is also used for the shift shading on the price chart. The default gets a little darker on light chart themes. A color you pick is used as-is.

inputs.title: Noise Lookback
inputs.tooltip: How many bars the filter uses to learn what a normal surprise looks like. Shorter adapts to new volatility faster, so the Surprise meter reacts quicker and fades sooner. Longer gives a steadier idea of normal, so a real change in volatility stands out for longer.

inputs.title: Trend Centering
inputs.tooltip: Subtracts the average surprise before testing each bar, so a steady trend is not mistaken for noise. Turned off, the line's normal lag in a strong trend counts as surprise, which means more dots and a higher Surprise meter. Most people should leave this on.

inputs.title: Damping Meter
inputs.tooltip:
Damping is how much the filter holds its line back instead of chasing an unusual move. Think of a shock absorber. When price lands far from the prediction (a dot), the filter gives that price less weight, so the line only moves part of the way toward it.

The Damping meter is the line below zero. It shows how much less the filter line is reacting than it normally would. 0 means no damping. A dip only starts on a dotted bar, then fades over the next several bars as the filter trusts price again.

Two settings shape it. Unusual-Move Threshold decides how often it dips. Damping Strength decides how deep each dip goes and how long it lasts.

The color is also used for the glow around the filter line. The default gets a little darker on light chart themes. A color you pick is used as-is.

inputs.title: Unusual-Move Threshold
inputs.tooltip:
Decides which bars count as unusual moves, and so how often the Damping meter dips.

Every bar, the filter checks how far price landed from its prediction and compares that with a typical surprise. If it is more than this many times a typical surprise, the bar is an unusual move. It gets a dot, and it gets damped. At 2, price has to land twice as far from the prediction as usual.

Lower gives more dots, so the meter dips more often. Higher keeps only the biggest shocks. As a rough guide, at 1.5 about 1 bar in 7 gets a dot, at 2 about 1 in 20, and at 3 about 1 in 60 to 100.

How hard each dotted bar is damped is set by Damping Strength.

inputs.title: Damping Strength
inputs.tooltip:
Decides how hard each unusual move is damped, which sets how deep each dip in the Damping meter goes and how long it takes to fade.

Higher holds the filter line back harder when a shock hits, so the line ignores more of it. The trade-off is that when the move turns out to be real, the line takes longer to catch up.

This is not a percentage. At the same setting, a bigger miss is damped harder. As a rough guide, one dot makes the meter dip to about:
0.05: 15 to 25, fading in about 10 bars
0.1: 25 to 40, fading in about 20 bars
0.3: 50 to 70, fading in about 40 bars

At 0 nothing is damped. The dots still show, but the meter stays near zero and no volatility shifts are marked.

Which bars get dots is set by the Unusual-Move Threshold.

inputs.title: Glow Around the Filter Line
inputs.tooltip: Lights up a soft band around the filter line on the price chart while it is being damped. Brighter means the line is being held back more.

inputs.title: Filter Line on Price Chart
inputs.tooltip: Draws the filter line on the price chart, teal while it is rising and red while it is falling. Turning it off also hides the glow.

inputs.title: Line Color Hold
inputs.tooltip:
How far the filter line has to come back off its latest high or low before it changes color, measured in typical bar moves. This only changes the color, not the line.

At 0 the line changes color on every small wiggle, which in a sideways market can mean a color change every few bars. At 0.25 it changes about a third as often. Higher holds the color through bigger pullbacks, but a real turn shows up a bar or two later.

inputs.title: Shift Shading on Price Chart
inputs.tooltip: Shades the price chart and the pane during a volatility shift, from its start until it settles: the market is noisier than normal and the filter is actively damping the line. A shift starts when the blue and gray meters have both crossed their dashed shift level in the pane. The shading follows the smaller of the two meters, so it is strongest while both are high and fades as either one fades.

inputs.title: Halo on Unusual Moves
inputs.tooltip:
Puts a soft oval of light behind each candle that crossed the Unusual-Move Threshold, teal for a move up and red for a move down. It does not redraw the candle or its wick. Only the last 100 unusual moves get one.

Hover the middle of a marked candle to see how big the move was and how much the line was damped.

inputs.title: Unusual-Move Dots on Price Chart
inputs.tooltip:
Puts a small dot slightly below or above each candle that crossed the Unusual-Move Threshold, leaving room around the wick. Teal marks a move up and red marks a move down. Hover a dot to see how big the move was and how much the line was damped.

This is separate from the halo, so you can show either one, both, or neither.

inputs.title: Unusual-Move Dots in Pane
inputs.tooltip: Marks each unusual move with a dot on the oscillator's center line, teal for a move up and red for a move down. This is separate from how unusual moves are marked on the price chart, so either one can be turned off on its own.

inputs.title: Input 17
inputs.tooltip: Where the readout sits on the price chart. It is drawn there so it never covers the oscillator. Hover the state name for what it means.
